Rashi on Bekhorot 2b:10:1.english: Which may come to be confused - To permit the sale of an unblemished [animal].

Rashi on Bekhorot 2b:11:1.english: Which is separated from him - That he did not retain anything in it for himself once he sold it.

Rashi on Bekhorot 2b:11:2.hebrew: וכ"ש שלמה - כי האי גוונא דלא פסקה מיניה, שהרי שייר לעצמו גוף הבהמה. ואי משום עוברין — ליכא למיחש, שהרי לא נתעברה עדיין, ולא כלום מכר לו, ולכשיבאו — ברשות עובד כוכבים הם באים:
Rashi on Bekhorot 2b:11:2.english: And all the more so an unblemished [animal] - In a case like this, where it is not separated from him, for he retained for himself the body of the animal. And if [one might be concerned] on account of the fetuses, there is no concern, for it has not yet conceived and he did not sell him anything; and when they come [into the world], they come into the possession of the gentile.

Rashi on Bekhorot 2b:12:1.hebrew: דפסקה מיניה - ומכירה חלוטה היא, ואתי לאחלופי ולהתיר מכירה חלוטה שלמה. אבל הכא, דלא פסקה מיניה — שרי, דלאו מכירה היא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 2b:12:1.english: As it is separated from him - And it is an outright sale, and [people] will come to confuse [it] and permit the outright sale of an intact [animal]. But here, where it is not separated from him, it is permitted, as it is not [considered] a sale.

Rashi on Bekhorot 2b:13:1.english: And all the more so an unblemished [animal], which is liable to be confused - With an outright sale of another unblemished [animal].

Rashi on Bekhorot 2b:14:1.hebrew: משום הכי הוא - בתמיה, דאיצטריך לן למיבעי:
Rashi on Bekhorot 2b:14:1.english: Is it due to that - [This is asked] in astonishment: [Is that really their reason,] that it was necessary for us to raise the dilemma?

Rashi on Bekhorot 2b:14:3.hebrew:
אלמא - טעמא דרבנן משום עוברין, תיפשוט מינה דלרבנן אסור למכור לעובד כוכבים בהמה לעובריה, ולר' יהודה מותר:
לעולם טעמא דרבנן משום איחלופי, ואיצטריך למיבעי: כיון דלא פסקה מיניה, איכא למימר לא אתי לאיחלופי במכירה גמורה. והכי קאמרי ליה רבנן לר' יהודה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 2b:14:3.english:
Apparently - The reason of the Rabbis is due to fetuses; resolve from it that according to the Rabbis it is forbidden to sell an animal to a gentile for its fetuses, and according to Rabbi Yehuda it is permitted.
Actually, the reason of the Rabbis is due to [concern of] confusion, and it was necessary to raise the dilemma: Since it is not completely separated from him, one could say that people will not come to confuse it with a complete sale. And this is what the Rabbis were saying to Rabbi Yehuda:

Rashi on Bekhorot 2b:15:1.hebrew: כמאן דזבנה לשחיטה דמי - וליכא למיחש לאיחלופי, דמאן דחזי ידע דלא מזבין ליה אלא לשחיטה, ולא אתי לזבוני בהמה שלא לשחיטה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 2b:15:1.english: It is considered like one who sold it for slaughter - And there is no concern about confusion, for whoever sees [it] knows that he is selling it only for slaughter, and one will not come to sell an animal [that is] not for slaughter.

Rashi on Bekhorot 2b:16:1.hebrew: משהא לה - לצורך וולדות, ומאן דחזי לה בבית העובד כוכבים לסוף שנה או שתים, סבר: מותר למכור בהמה לעובד כוכבים שלא לשחיטה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 2b:16:1.english: He delays it - For the sake of offspring, and one who sees it in the house of the gentile after a year or two will think: It is permitted to sell an animal to a gentile not for slaughter.

Rashi on Bekhorot 2b:18:1.english: Come and hear - From our mishna.

Rashi on Bekhorot 2b:18:2.hebrew: ולא קתני אע"פ שאינו רשאי - אלמא מותר למכור בהמה לעובריה, דהא קבלה מכירה לעוברין היא, שאין חולק העובד כוכבים אלא בוולדות — דקס"ד דלא פליג עובד כוכבים בשבח פטימת בהמה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 2b:18:2.english: And it does not teach: Although he is not permitted - Evidently, it is permitted to sell an animal for its fetuses, as receivership is a sale for fetuses, since the gentile shares only in the offspring — for it entered [the Gemara's] mind that the gentile does not share in the increase in value from the fattening of the animal.

Rashi on Bekhorot 2b:19:1.english: Out of your mouth - Through your mouth causing [it].

Rashi on Bekhorot 2b:1:1.english: What, is it not regarding the fetus - [That] it says that he is not permitted?

Rashi on Bekhorot 2b:20:1.hebrew: תנא במכירה - אינו רשאי, והוא הדין לכולהו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 2b:20:1.english: [The Tanna] taught in [the case of] sale - [That] he is not permitted, and the same law applies to all of them.

Rashi on Bekhorot 2b:20:2.hebrew: ומאי שנא מכירה דנקט - בה אינו רשאי, ולא נקטיה בחדא מהנך:
Rashi on Bekhorot 2b:20:2.english: And what is different about selling that he cited [it] - [That] regarding it [he stated], “he is not permitted,” and he did not cite it regarding one of those [other cases].

Rashi on Bekhorot 2b:20:3.english: That the primary [case] is sale - The primary prohibition is the sale of an animal.

Rashi on Bekhorot 2b:2:1.hebrew: כהן מאי עבידתיה - בבהמה? אלא ודאי אעובר:
Rashi on Bekhorot 2b:2:1.english: What is the relevance of the priest - [What relevance does he have] to the animal? Rather, certainly [the penalty is] regarding the fetus.

Rashi on Bekhorot 2b:2:2.hebrew: לא - לעולם מהכא לא תפשוט, דהכא במאי עסקינן? כגון דיהיב ליה בהמה מעברתא לפטומה וליטול חצי השבח — בין בפטום בין בוולדות — דמיגו דקנסינן וכו'. אבל אי זבין ליה עובר לחודיה — לא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 2b:2:2.english: No - Actually, you cannot resolve [the question] from here, for with what are we dealing here? For example, where he gave him a pregnant animal to fatten it and to take half the increase — both in [its] fattening and in the offspring — so that “since we penalize [him for the animal, we penalize him for the fetus]...”; but if he sold him the fetus alone, [we do] not [penalize him].

Rashi on Bekhorot 2b:3:1.english: Because it is incapable of being cured - And [of] performing labor on Shabbat.

Rashi on Bekhorot 2b:4:1.english: Permits in [the case of] a damaged [animal] - And a fetus is similar to a damaged [animal].

Rashi on Bekhorot 2b:5:1.english: It is its natural way - And it is not [considered] damaged.

Rashi on Bekhorot 2b:9:1.hebrew: בהמה לעובריה - כגון שעדיין לא נתעברה, ומכר לו כל הוולדות שעתידין להתעבר, ובהמה עצמה לא מכר לו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 2b:9:1.english: An animal for its fetuses - For example, where it has not yet become pregnant, and he sold him all the offspring that are destined to be conceived, but the animal itself he did not sell him.

Rashi on Bekhorot 2b:9:2.english: What is [the ruling] - [Is it] to penalize him [by requiring him] to redeem it, on account of [the law of] one who sells an animal to a gentile?

Tosafot on Bekhorot 2b:17:1.hebrew: דלא מקבלת זכר - לא מטעם טרפות, מדאמר פרק אלו טריפות (חולין דף נז:) גבי ר"ש [בן חלפתא] שהיה עסקן בדברים: "ודילמא קסבר ר' יהודה טריפה יולדת ומשבחת". ואית ספרים דלא גרסי "יולדת", שאין צורך שם בלידה, אלא במה שמשבחת. ומ"מ מסתבר הכא, דאפילו מן הארכובה ולמטה שרי רבי יהודה, משום דלא מקבלה זכר:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 2b:17:1.english: "As it does not accept a male" - [This is] not on account of [its being a] tereifah, as [the Gemara] says in the chapter Elu Tereifot (Chullin 57b) regarding Rabbi Shimon [ben Ḥalafta], who was an investigator of matters: "And perhaps Rabbi Yehuda holds that a tereifah gives birth and improves?" And there are texts that do not read "gives birth," as there is no need there for [a reference to] giving birth, but only for [the fact] that it improves. And nevertheless, it is reasonable [to say] here that even [if the break is] from the knee downward, Rabbi Yehuda permits [selling it], because it does not accept a male.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 2b:19:1.hebrew: ולטעמיך המשתתף לו כו' - מקבלה לא שייך להקשות דמיתסר משום שותפין, דלא אתי בקבלה כל כך לידי שבועה. ודוקא נקט שותפות, אבל שאר משא ומתן לא אסור:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 2b:19:1.english: "But according to your reasoning, one who enters into a partnership with him, etc." - From [the case of] receivership, it is not applicable to raise an objection that it should be prohibited on account of partnership, since in receivership one does not come so [readily] to an oath; and [Shmuel's father] specifically stated "partnership," but other business dealings are not prohibited.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 2b:19:2.hebrew: אסור לאדם שיעשה שותפות עם העובד כוכבים - הא דתניא פ"ק דמסכת ע"ז (דף כב.): "ישראל ועובד כוכבים שקבלו שדה בשותפות", וכן עובדא דעובד כוכבים נוטל שני ערלה וישראל נוטל שני היתר, ואמר פרק הזרוע (חולין דף קלג.): "המשתתף עם עובד כוכבים צריך שירשום" — כל הני עובדא פליגי אאבוה דשמואל:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 2b:19:2.english: "It is prohibited for a person to enter into a partnership with a gentile" - That which is taught in a baraita in the first chapter of tractate Avodah Zarah (22a): "A Jew and a gentile who received a field in partnership," and similarly the incident where the gentile takes the years of orlah and the Jew takes the permitted years, and [that which] the chapter [entitled] Hazeroa states (Chullin 133a): "One who enters into partnership with a gentile must mark [his animal]" — all these cases disagree with Shmuel's father.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 2b:19:3.hebrew: שמא יתחייב לו עובד כוכבים שבועה - מכאן אוסר רבינו שמואל קבלת השבועה מק"ו, ור"ת מתיר, מפני שהוא כמציל מידם; כדתניא פ"ק דמס' ע"ז (דף ו:): מלוה על פה גובין מהן מפני שהוא כמציל מידם, אע"ג דאזיל ומודה. ויש לחלק בין ספק לודאי. עוד מייתי ר"ת ראיה מההיא דפרק [בתרא] דמגילה (דף כח.), דאמר אבוה בר איהי: "תיתי לי דלא עבדי שותפות עם עובד כוכבים"; ואי אסור, מאי רבותיה? וכן פר"ת שלא היו נזהרים משלש סעודות, מדאמר פרק כל כתבי (שבת דף קיח:): "תיתי לי דקיימית ג' סעודות", משמע שכולן לא היו נזהרים בהן. עוד פר"ת: בזמן הזה כולן נשבעים בקדשים ואין תופסין בהם אלהות, ואע"פ שמזכירין [עמהם] שם שמים וכוונתם [לד"א מ"מ], אין זה [שם] עבודת כוכבים, כי דעתם לשם עושה שמים וארץ. ואע"ג שמשתתף ש"ש ודבר אחר, אין כאן "לפני עור לא תתן מכשול", דבני נח לא הוזהרו על כך; ולדידן לא אשכחן איסור בגרם שיתוף:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 2b:19:3.english: "Lest the idolater become obligated to take an oath to him" - From here, Rabbeinu Shmuel prohibits accepting the oath [from the gentile] through an a fortiori inference (kal va-chomer), and Rabbeinu Tam permits [it], because it is like rescuing [one's property] from their hands, as is taught in a baraita in the first chapter of Tractate Avodah Zarah (6b): A loan by oral agreement may be collected from them, because it is like rescuing [one's property] from their hands, even though he will go and give thanks [to his idol]. And one can distinguish between [a case of] uncertainty and [a case of] certainty. Further, Rabbeinu Tam brings proof from that [passage] in the [last] chapter of Megillah (28a), where Avuha bar Ihi said: "May [a reward] come to me, for I never entered into a partnership with an idolater." And if it is [strictly] prohibited, what is his greatness? And similarly, Rabbeinu Tam explained that they [the general public] were not careful regarding three meals [on Shabbat], since it is stated in the chapter "Kol Kitvei" (Shabbat 118b): "May [a reward] come to me, for I fulfilled three meals [on Shabbat]," which implies that not everyone was careful about them. Further, Rabbeinu Tam explained: Nowadays, they all swear by their holy beings [i.e., the saints] and they do not view them as deities; and even though they mention the Name of Heaven along [with them] and their intention is [also for something else, nevertheless,] this is not [the name of] idolatry, for their intention is to the Name of the Maker of heaven and earth. And even though he associates the Name of Heaven with something else, there is no [violation of] "You shall not put a stumbling block before the blind" here, for the descendants of Noah were not prohibited against this [association]; and as for us, we have not found a prohibition against causing association.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 2b:1:1.hebrew: מאי לאו אעובר - פי': ואיירי בבהמה מעוברת. "לא, אבהמה" — פי': ולא איירי בעובר, אלא בבהמה לעוברה. וכן משמע לקמן, גבי בעיא ד"בהמה לעובריה מהו", ובעי למיפשט מהכא דאסור, דקאמר: "מאי לאו אבהמה?" — ש"מ דאי אבהמה קאי, איירי בבהמה לעוברה. ולכאורה לא איירי בבהמה לעוברה, דא"כ מאי פריך: "והא דמיו קתני"? לימא דקאי אעובר! וכי תימא דמשמע ליה דקאי אבהמה — א"כ, לקמן נמי לידוק הכי! אלא הכא איירי בבהמה לפטומה, כדמסיק; לקמן — לעוברה:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 2b:1:1.english: "What, is it not referring to the fetus?" - Explanation: That is, it is dealing with a pregnant animal. "No, [it is referring] to the animal" — Explanation: And it is not dealing with an [existing] fetus, but rather with an animal [given] for its [future] offspring. And so it is implied below (3a) regarding the inquiry: "An animal for its offspring, what is [the ruling]?" — where [the Gemara] seeks to resolve from here that it is forbidden, as it says: "What, is it not referring to the animal?" Learn from it that if it refers to the animal, it is dealing with an animal [given] for its offspring. Yet seemingly, [here] it is not dealing with an animal for its offspring, for if so, why does [the Gemara] object: "But doesn't it teach: 'its value' [damav, in the masculine]?" Let [the Gemara] say that [the word damav] refers to the fetus! And if you would say that it was evident to [the Gemara] that it refers to the animal — if so, below too let it make this inference! Rather, here [on 2b] it is dealing with an animal for fattening, as it concludes; [whereas] below [on 3a, it is dealing with an animal given] for its offspring.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 2b:20:1.hebrew: דעיקר מכירה - פרש"י: דעיקר איסור הוא המכירה — משמע שרוצה לומר שעיקר האיסור הוא המכירה. וקשה: הא שותפות לא מיתסר משום מכירה, אלא כדאבוה דשמואל! וצ"ל: עיקר איסור הפשוט הוא מכירה, כדתנן פרק קמא דמס' ע"ז (דף יד:):
Tosafot on Bekhorot 2b:20:1.english: "That the primary [prohibition] is selling" - Rashi explained that the primary prohibition is the sale — which implies that he means to say that the primary prohibition is the sale [itself]. And [this] is difficult: for surely partnership is not prohibited on account of sale, but rather in accordance with [the statement of] Shmuel's father! And one must say: The primary, straightforward prohibition is sale, as we learned in the first chapter of Tractate Avodah Zarah (14b) [that one may not sell large livestock to them].
